quote:
I am a freelance comic book artist/illustrator and a sole proprietor living in the city. The removal of the $100,000 BIRT exemption for the 2025 tax year caught me and even my CPA a bit by surprise. I was thankfully able to pay it from some of the savings I have in my business account. But it was definitely a hit to my finances I wasn't anticipating. I owed ~$1,800 that I'd otherwise be spending on new equipment, or possibly even groceries and other bills if work and payments get a little infrequent as I'm not always paid every month.

The $100,000 BIRT exemption was a huge boon to people like me and I find it unconscionable that myself and my fellow artists and sole proprietors/single-member LLC's who are often in precarious financial situations are being forced to pay even more in taxes when we're already being squeezed to our limit. This needs to be remedied in a way that restores the $100,000 exemption or something similar.

quote: I love Philadelphia, but my business can be run two miles away, nearby, and I won’t have to pay BIRT ($4,400 last year). We are being double taxed. We already pay our fair NPT tax which, incidentally, is not seemingly used to create a reliable and working public transit system so no one who lives here can get to my business in the first place reliably. Ultimately, if the BIRT doesn’t change, NJ is waiting with open arms, which I don’t want to do, but may have to.
